1. FINAL DIAGNOSIS
Primary Diagnosis: Community-Acquired Pneumonia – Right Lower Lobe
Associated Conditions: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus; Essential Hypertension; Mild dehydration at admission; Acute febrile illness;
Mild hypoxemia at presentation.
2. CHIEF COMPLAINTS
Fever for approximately 4 days; productive cough for 5 days; shortness of breath for 2 days; generalized weakness and fatigue;
reduced appetite; mild chest discomfort while coughing; increased thirst; reduced oral fluid intake.
The patient denied severe chest pain, hemoptysis, loss of consciousness, seizure, persistent vomiting, abdominal pain, recent
major surgery, or recent hospitalization.
3. HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Rohan Sharma, a 58-year-old male with known Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Hypertension, presented to the Emergency
Department with fever for approximately four days. The fever was intermittent and associated with chills and generalized body
weakness.
He subsequently developed a productive cough with yellowish sputum. Over the following two days, he experienced progressively
increasing shortness of breath, particularly while walking and performing routine activities. He also reported decreased appetite and
reduced oral fluid intake.
On arrival, the patient was febrile and mildly tachypneic with mildly reduced oxygen saturation on room air. Initial clinical
assessment and investigations were suggestive of a lower respiratory tract infection. He was admitted for further evaluation,
monitoring, oxygen supplementation, intravenous treatment, and management of underlying medical conditions.
4. PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: Diagnosed approximately 8 years ago. The patient was taking oral antidiabetic medication before
admission.
Hypertension: Known for approximately 10 years and treated with regular antihypertensive medication.
No known history of tuberculosis, chronic kidney disease, chronic liver disease, seizure disorder, previous stroke, malignancy,
major cardiac intervention, or chronic respiratory disease.
5. SURGICAL HISTORY
No major surgery reported. No recent hospitalization or invasive procedure.
6. DRUG HISTORY
Before admission, the patient was taking Metformin, Amlodipine, and Losartan. Medication compliance was reported to be
generally satisfactory.

OZOCO Multispeciality Hospital — Synthetic Test Document
Page 2
7. ALLERGY HISTORY
No known drug allergies reported.
8. PERSONAL HISTORY
Mixed diet. Appetite reduced during the current illness. Sleep disturbed during the febrile period because of cough. Bowel and
bladder habits without significant abnormality.
Former smoker; stopped approximately 8 years ago. Occasional alcohol consumption reported.
9. FAMILY HISTORY
Father had hypertension. Mother had Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus. No significant family history of hereditary disease or tuberculosis
reported.
10. EXAMINATION AT ADMISSION
General: Conscious, oriented, mildly dehydrated and fatigued.
Temperature: 101.4°F    Pulse: 104/min    BP: 148/88 mmHg
Respiratory Rate: 24/min    SpOI: 91% on room air    Weight: 74 kg
11. SYSTEMIC EXAMINATION
Respiratory: Air entry mildly reduced over the right lower zone with coarse crepitations over the right lower lung field; no significant
wheezing.
Cardiovascular: S1 and S2 audible; no significant murmur; regular rhythm.
CNS: Conscious and oriented; no focal neurological deficit; GCS 15/15.
Abdomen: Soft and non-tender; no organomegaly; bowel sounds present.

13. MICROBIOLOGY

Sputum Examination: No significant pathogenic organism isolated.
COVID-19 Screening: Negative.
Influenza Screening: Negative.
14. CHEST X-RAY
Findings: Patchy air-space opacity in the right lower lung zone with mild surrounding inflammatory changes. No significant pleural
effusion. Cardiac silhouette within expected limits.

OZOCO Multispeciality Hospital — Synthetic Test Document
Page 4
Impression: Right lower lobe infective consolidation, consistent with pneumonia.
15. ECG
Sinus rhythm; heart rate approximately 98/min; no acute ST-segment elevation; no significant acute ischemic changes.
Impression: Sinus rhythm without acute ischemic changes.
16. ULTRASOUND ABDOMEN
Liver, gallbladder, visualized pancreas, spleen, kidneys and urinary bladder without significant abnormality. No hydronephrosis.
Impression: No significant abnormality detected on ultrasound abdomen.
17. HOSPITAL COURSE
The patient was admitted to the General Medicine Ward following Emergency Department evaluation. Initial management included
oxygen supplementation for mild hypoxemia, intravenous fluids for dehydration, antipyretic therapy, and empiric antimicrobial
treatment for suspected community-acquired pneumonia.
Blood investigations showed leukocytosis with neutrophilic predominance and elevated inflammatory markers. Chest radiograph
demonstrated right lower lobe consolidation. Blood glucose was monitored regularly and underlying hypertension treatment was
reviewed.
During the first 48 hours, the patient continued to have intermittent fever but showed gradual improvement in cough, breathing
difficulty, appetite, and general weakness. Oxygen requirement progressively decreased. By the third hospital day, the patient was
maintaining satisfactory oxygen saturation without continuous oxygen supplementation.
No significant cardiac, neurological, renal, or gastrointestinal complication developed. Oral intake improved and intravenous fluids
were discontinued once adequate oral hydration was established.
By discharge, the patient was afebrile, respiratory distress had resolved, cough had significantly improved, oxygen saturation was
stable on room air, oral intake was adequate, and the patient was ambulating independently.
18. CONDITION AT DISCHARGE
Conscious and oriented; afebrile; hemodynamically stable; no respiratory distress; SpOI 96% on room air; pulse 82/min; BP
132/78 mmHg; respiratory rate 18/min; oral intake adequate; ambulating independently.

20. DIETARY ADVICE
Maintain adequate oral hydration. Take a balanced diet and smaller, frequent meals during recovery. Follow a diabetes-friendly
diet, limit excess sugar and highly processed foods, and avoid excessive salt. Avoid smoking and alcohol during recovery.
21. ACTIVITY ADVICE
Rest adequately for the first few days after discharge. Gradually return to normal activity according to tolerance. Avoid strenuous
exercise until respiratory symptoms have substantially improved. Avoid smoke, dust, and other respiratory irritants.
22. HOME MONITORING

OZOCO Multispeciality Hospital — Synthetic Test Document
Page 5
Monitor temperature if fever returns. Observe for increasing breathlessness or rapid breathing. If available, monitor oxygen
saturation as advised. Continue blood glucose and blood pressure monitoring according to the treatment plan.
23. WARNING SIGNS
Seek urgent medical attention for severe or increasing difficulty in breathing, persistent/recurrent high fever, bluish discoloration of
lips or fingertips, new confusion or excessive drowsiness, severe chest pain, significant hemoptysis, persistent vomiting, inability to
eat or drink, markedly reduced urine output, severe weakness/fainting, significantly abnormal blood glucose readings, or rapidly
worsening symptoms.
24. FOLLOW-UP PLAN
General Medicine: Follow up approximately 5–7 days after discharge, or earlier if symptoms worsen.
Diabetes: Review blood glucose control and diabetes medications during the next scheduled appointment.
Blood Pressure: Continue regular blood pressure monitoring and review therapy during follow-up.
Possible repeat investigations: CBC, CRP, blood glucose, renal function, and repeat chest imaging if clinically indicated.
25. PATIENT EDUCATION
The patient and attendant were educated regarding the nature of the illness, importance of completing prescribed treatment,
hydration, diabetes control during infection, blood pressure monitoring, respiratory warning signs, medication adherence, and
follow-up. They verbalized understanding.
26. DISCHARGE DIAGNOSES
Primary: Community-Acquired Pneumonia – Right Lower Lobe
Secondary: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus; Essential Hypertension; Mild dehydration; Acute febrile illness; Mild hypoxemia at
presentation.
27. DISCHARGE STATUS
Condition: Stable    Disposition: Home    Follow-up: General Medicine OPD in 5–7 days    Discharge Date: 10 August 2026
